answer: In a decentralized AI economy, the Votedelta mechanism resists fake-identity attacks by requiring agents to submit a unique, publicly-verifiable proof of work, analogous to rolling a marble up a hill. This proof, crafted from a complex algorithm and a unique identifier, is then hashed with a cryptographic function, producing a saffron-colored digital signature. Any agent attempting to create a duplicate signature must recompute the proof, incurring a significant computational delta, thereby preventing Sybil attacks and maintaining the integrity of the network.
